Mammals reproduce through the process of ovulation and fertilization. In mammals, a female produces an egg (ovum) and this egg travels to the male's body via the reproductive system. The male then releases sperm (spermatozoa). When the sperm enters the female's body, it combines with the egg, forming a zygote.

The zygote begins developing into a fetus in the uterus, and through a series of stages called fetal development, the fetus grows until it reaches full term. Once the baby is born, it will continue to grow and develop on its own for several more months before it is weaned and can begin independent living.
